title: Syntax that says a lot
description: Small symbols with a big meaning: ?, ??, ?., =>, $"", records, pattern matching and switch expressions.

content.title: Small symbols, big meaning
content.body:
C# packs a lot of meaning into a few symbols:
- string? name: name may be null.
- a ?? b: a, or b if a is null.
- user?.Name: user.Name, or null if user is null (instead of crashing).
- x => x * 2: a lambda, a small function written inline.
- $"Hello {name}": an interpolated string, with name inserted in the text.

They make code short, but you have to read them carefully.

choices.text: null
It throws a NullReferenceException
It does not compile

content.explanation: name?.Length gives null because name is null, and ?? 0 replaces that null with 0. No exception: that is exactly what ?. and ?? are for.

choices.text: Hello Ada, 2 messages
Hello {name}, {1 + 1} messages
Hello Ada, 1 + 1 messages
$Hello Ada, 2 messages

content.explanation: The $ prefix makes an interpolated string: each {expression} is evaluated and inserted in the text.

content.question:
int Double(int x) => x * 2;

What does => mean here?

choices.text: The method's body is the expression x * 2: it returns x * 2
"Greater than or equal to"
x is passed by reference
The result is assigned to x

content.explanation: This is an expression-bodied member: a shorter way to write { return x * 2; }. The same arrow is used in lambdas such as x => x * 2. "Greater than or equal to" is written >=.

content.question:
int? score = null;

What is int?

choices.text: An int that can also be null
An int whose value is not known yet at compile time
A pointer to an int
A syntax error: int can never be null

content.explanation: int? is short for Nullable<int>. A plain int always has a value; int? adds null, useful for "no score yet".

content.title: Modern C#
content.body:
Recent versions of C# added features that make code shorter and clearer:
- Records: record Point(int X, int Y); creates a small immutable type in one line, compared by value.
- Pattern matching: if (shape is Circle c) tests the type and gives you a variable of that type.
- Switch expressions: choose a value from patterns, with _ for "anything else".
- using declarations: using var file = ...; disposes the file automatically at the end of the block.

choices.text: It does not compile: _ is not a valid pattern

content.explanation: The patterns are tested in order: 75 is not >= 90, but it is >= 70, so the result is "B". _ is the discard pattern, which matches anything.

choices.text: true: records are compared by their values
false: they are two different objects
It does not compile: == cannot compare records
true, but only because the numbers are small

content.explanation: Records have value equality: two records are equal when all their properties are equal. For a normal class, == would compare the references and give false.

choices.text: Checks that shape is a Circle and, if so, gives it to you as c, typed Circle
Converts any shape into a new Circle
Checks that shape and c are the same object
Declares a Circle named c, whatever shape is

content.explanation: This is a type pattern: the test and the cast in one step. Inside the if, c is a Circle, so c.Radius compiles.
